description_full: GFL Environmental Inc. provides non-hazardous solid waste management services in Canada and the United States. It offers solid waste management services, including collection, transportation, transfer, recycling, and disposal services for municipal, residential, commercial, and industrial customers. The company was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Miami Beach, Florida.

financial_summary: GFL Environmental Inc. Subordin is a large-cap industrials business with a $18.5B market cap on $4.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +6.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 0% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $122M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.35×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
Accruals are elevated at +12.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 10.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 11.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.5% of the shares.
